all.help: Automatically stage files that have been modified and deleted, but new files you have not told Git about are not affected

allow_empty.help: Usually recording a commit that has the exact same tree as its sole parent commit is a mistake, and the command prevents you from making such a commit

allow_empty_message.help: Create a commit with an empty commit message without using plumbing commands like git-commit-tree(1)

amend.help: Replace the tip of the current branch by creating a new commit

branch.help: Show the branch and tracking info even in short-format

cleanup.help: Determine how the supplied commit message should be cleaned up before committing

date.help: Override the author date used in the commit

dry_run.help: Do not create a commit, but show a list of paths that are to be committed, paths with local changes that will be left uncommitted and paths that are untracked

edit.help: Let the user further edit the message taken from <file> with -F <file>, command line with -m <message>, and from <commit> with -C <commit>

fixup.help: Create a new commit which "fixes up" <commit> when applied with git rebase --autosquash

include.help: Before making a commit out of staged contents so far, stage the contents of paths given on the command line as well

inter_hunk_context.help: Show the context between diff hunks, up to the specified <number> of lines, thereby fusing hunks that are close to each other

long.help: When doing a dry-run, give the output in the long-format

null.help: When showing short or porcelain git-status(1) output, print the filename verbatim and terminate the entries with NUL, instead of LF

only.help: Make a commit by taking the updated working tree contents of the paths specified on the command line, disregarding any contents that have been staged for other paths

patch.help: Use the interactive patch selection interface to choose which changes to commit

pathspec_from_file.help: Pass pathspec in <file> instead of commandline args

porcelain.help: When doing a dry-run, give the output in a porcelain-ready format

reedit_message.help: Like -C, but with -c the editor is invoked, so that the user can further edit the commit message

reset_author.help: When used with -C/-c/--amend options, or when committing after a conflicting cherry-pick, declare that the authorship of the resulting commit now belongs to the committer

reuse_message.help: Take an existing <commit> object, and reuse the log message and the authorship information (including the timestamp) when creating the commit

short.help: When doing a dry-run, give the output in the short-format

signoff.help: Add a Signed-off-by trailer by the committer at the end of the commit log message

squash.help: Construct a commit message for use with git rebase --autosquash

status.help: Include the output of git-status(1) in the commit message template when using an editor to prepare the commit message

template.help: When editing the commit message, start the editor with the contents in <file>

trailer.help: Specify a (<token>, <value>) pair that should be applied as a trailer

unified.help: Generate diffs with <n> lines of context

verbose.help: Show unified diff between the HEAD commit and what would be committed at the bottom of the commit message template to help the user describe the commit by reminding what changes the commit has

verify.help: Bypass the pre-commit and commit-msg hooks

fetch.help: Download objects and refs from another repository

all.help: Fetch all remotes, except for the ones that has the remote.<name>.skipFetchAll configuration variable set

append.help: Append ref names and object names of fetched refs to the existing contents of .git/FETCH_HEAD

atomic.help: Use an atomic transaction to update local refs

auto_maintenance.help: Run git maintenance run --auto at the end to perform automatic repository maintenance if needed

deepen.help: Similar to --depth, except it specifies the number of commits from the current shallow boundary instead of from the tip of each remote branch history

depth.help: Limit fetching to the specified number of commits from the tip of each remote branch history

dry_run.help: Show what would be done, without making any changes

force.help: When git fetch is used with <src>:<dst> refspec, it may refuse to update the local branch as discussed in the <refspec> part below

ipv4.help: Use IPv4 addresses only, ignoring IPv6 addresses

ipv6.help: Use IPv6 addresses only, ignoring IPv4 addresses

jobs.help: Parallelize all forms of fetching up to <n> jobs at a time

multiple.help: Allow several <repository> and <group> arguments to be specified

negotiate_only.help: Do not fetch anything from the server, and instead print the ancestors of the provided --negotiation-tip= arguments, which we have in common with the server

negotiation_tip.help: By default, Git will report, to the server, commits reachable from all local refs to find common commits in an attempt to reduce the size of the to-be-received packfile

no_recurse_submodules.help: Disable recursive fetching of submodules (this has the same effect as using the --recurse-submodules=no option)

porcelain.help: Print the output to standard output in an easy-to-parse format for scripts

prefetch.help: Modify the configured refspec to place all refs into the refs/prefetch/ namespace

progress.help: Progress status is reported on the standard error stream by default when it is attached to a terminal, unless -q is specified

prune.help: Before fetching, remove any remote-tracking references that no longer exist on the remote

prune_tags.help: Before fetching, remove any local tags that no longer exist on the remote if --prune is enabled

quiet.help: Pass --quiet to git-fetch-pack and silence any other internally used git commands

recurse_submodules.help: Control if and under what conditions new commits of submodules should be fetched too

recurse_submodules_default.help: This option is used internally to temporarily provide a non-negative default value for the --recurse-submodules option

refetch.help: Instead of negotiating with the server to avoid transferring commits and associated objects that are already present locally, this option fetches all objects as a fresh clone would

refmap.help: When fetching refs listed on the command line, use the specified refspec (can be given more than once) to map the refs to remote-tracking branches, instead of the values of remote.<name>.fetch configuration variables for the remote repository

server_option.help: Transmit the given string to the server when communicating using protocol version 2

set_upstream.help: If the remote is fetched successfully, add upstream (tracking) reference, used by argument-less git-pull(1) and other commands

shallow_exclude.help: Deepen or shorten the history of a shallow repository to exclude commits reachable from a specified remote branch or tag

shallow_since.help: Deepen or shorten the history of a shallow repository to include all reachable commits after <date>

show_forced_updates.help: By default, git checks if a branch is force-updated during fetch

stdin.help: Read refspecs, one per line, from stdin in addition to those provided as arguments

submodule_prefix.help: Prepend <path> to paths printed in informative messages such as "Fetching submodule foo"

tags.help: Fetch all tags from the remote (i.e., fetch remote tags refs/tags/* into local tags with the same name), in addition to whatever else would otherwise be fetched

unshallow.help: If the source repository is complete, convert a shallow repository to a complete one, removing all the limitations imposed by shallow repositories

update_head_ok.help: By default git fetch refuses to update the head which corresponds to the current branch

update_shallow.help: By default when fetching from a shallow repository, git fetch refuses refs that require updating .git/shallow

upload_pack.help: When given, and the repository to fetch from is handled by git fetch-pack, --exec=<upload-pack> is passed to the command to specify non-default path for the command run on the other end

write_fetch_head.help: Write the list of remote refs fetched in the FETCH_HEAD file directly under $GIT_DIR

pull.help: Fetch from and integrate with another repository or a local branch

allow_unrelated_histories.help: By default, git merge command refuses to merge histories that do not share a common ancestor

append.help: Append ref names and object names of fetched refs to the existing contents of .git/FETCH_HEAD

atomic.help: Use an atomic transaction to update local refs

autostash.help: Automatically create a temporary stash entry before the operation begins, record it in the ref MERGE_AUTOSTASH and apply it after the operation ends

cleanup.help: This option determines how the merge message will be cleaned up before committing

compact_summary.help: Show a compact-summary at the end of the merge

deepen.help: Similar to --depth, except it specifies the number of commits from the current shallow boundary instead of from the tip of each remote branch history

depth.help: Limit fetching to the specified number of commits from the tip of each remote branch history

dry_run.help: Show what would be done, without making any changes

edit.help: Invoke an editor before committing successful mechanical merge to further edit the auto-generated merge message, so that the user can explain and justify the merge

ff.help: When merging rather than rebasing, specifies how a merge is handled when the merged-in history is already a descendant of the current history

ff_only.help: Only update to the new history if there is no divergent local history

force.help: When git fetch is used with <src>:<dst> refspec, it may refuse to update the local branch as discussed in the <refspec> part of the git-fetch(1) documentation

ipv4.help: Use IPv4 addresses only, ignoring IPv6 addresses

ipv6.help: Use IPv6 addresses only, ignoring IPv4 addresses

jobs.help: Parallelize all forms of fetching up to <n> jobs at a time

log.help: In addition to branch names, populate the log message with one-line descriptions from at most <n> actual commits that are being merged

negotiate_only.help: Do not fetch anything from the server, and instead print the ancestors of the provided --negotiation-tip= arguments, which we have in common with the server

negotiation_tip.help: By default, Git will report, to the server, commits reachable from all local refs to find common commits in an attempt to reduce the size of the to-be-received packfile

porcelain.help: Print the output to standard output in an easy-to-parse format for scripts

prefetch.help: Modify the configured refspec to place all refs into the refs/prefetch/ namespace

progress.help: Progress status is reported on the standard error stream by default when it is attached to a terminal, unless -q is specified

prune.help: Before fetching, remove any remote-tracking references that no longer exist on the remote

quiet.help: This is passed to both underlying git-fetch to squelch reporting of during transfer, and underlying git-merge to squelch output during merging

rebase.help: true rebase the current branch on top of the upstream branch after fetching

recurse_submodules.help: This option controls if new commits of populated submodules should be fetched, and if the working trees of active submodules should be updated, too (see git-fetch(1), git-config(1) and gitmodules(5))

refmap.help: When fetching refs listed on the command line, use the specified refspec (can be given more than once) to map the refs to remote-tracking branches, instead of the values of remote.<name>.fetch configuration variables for the remote repository

server_option.help: Transmit the given string to the server when communicating using protocol version 2

set_upstream.help: If the remote is fetched successfully, add upstream (tracking) reference, used by argument-less git-pull(1) and other commands

shallow_exclude.help: Deepen or shorten the history of a shallow repository to exclude commits reachable from a specified remote branch or tag

shallow_since.help: Deepen or shorten the history of a shallow repository to include all reachable commits after <date>

show_forced_updates.help: By default, git checks if a branch is force-updated during fetch

signoff.help: Add a Signed-off-by trailer by the committer at the end of the commit log message

squash.help: Produce the working tree and index state as if a real merge happened (except for the merge information), but do not actually make a commit, move the HEAD, or record $GIT_DIR/MERGE_HEAD (to cause the next git commit command to create a merge commit)

stat.help: Show a diffstat at the end of the merge

strategy.help: Use the given merge strategy; can be supplied more than once to specify them in the order they should be tried

strategy_option.help: Pass merge strategy specific option through to the merge strategy

summary.help: Synonyms to --stat and --no-stat; these are deprecated and will be removed in the future

tags.help: Fetch all tags from the remote (i.e., fetch remote tags refs/tags/* into local tags with the same name), in addition to whatever else would otherwise be fetched

unshallow.help: If the source repository is complete, convert a shallow repository to a complete one, removing all the limitations imposed by shallow repositories

update_shallow.help: By default when fetching from a shallow repository, git fetch refuses refs that require updating .git/shallow

upload_pack.help: When given, and the repository to fetch from is handled by git fetch-pack, --exec=<upload-pack> is passed to the command to specify non-default path for the command run on the other end

verify.help: By default, the pre-merge and commit-msg hooks are run

verify_signatures.help: Verify that the tip commit of the side branch being merged is signed with a valid key, i.e. a key that has a valid uid: in the default trust model, this means the signing key has been signed by a trusted key

push.help: Update remote refs along with associated objects

atomic.help: Use an atomic transaction on the remote side if available

delete.help: All listed refs are deleted from the remote repository

dry_run.help: Do everything except actually send the updates

follow_tags.help: Push all the refs that would be pushed without this option, and also push annotated tags in refs/tags that are missing from the remote but are pointing at commit-ish that are reachable from the refs being pushed

force.help: Usually, git push will refuse to update a branch that is not an ancestor of the commit being pushed

force_if_includes.help: Force an update only if the tip of the remote-tracking ref has been integrated locally

force_with_lease.help: Usually, git push refuses to update a remote ref that is not an ancestor of the local ref used to overwrite it

ipv4.help: Use IPv4 addresses only, ignoring IPv6 addresses

ipv6.help: Use IPv6 addresses only, ignoring IPv4 addresses

mirror.help: Instead of naming each ref to push, specifies that all refs under refs/ (which includes but is not limited to refs/heads/, refs/remotes/, and refs/tags/) be mirrored to the remote repository

no_recurse_submodules.help: May be used to make sure all submodule commits used by the revisions to be pushed are available on a remote-tracking branch

progress.help: Progress status is reported on the standard error stream by default when it is attached to a terminal, unless -q is specified

prune.help: Remove remote branches that don't have a local counterpart

push_option.help: Transmit the given string to the server, which passes them to the pre-receive as well as the post-receive hook

quiet.help: Suppress all output, including the listing of updated refs, unless an error occurs

receive_pack.help: Path to the git-receive-pack program on the remote end

repo.help: This option is equivalent to the <repository> argument

set_upstream.help: For every branch that is up to date or successfully pushed, add upstream (tracking) reference, used by argument-less git-pull(1) and other commands

signed.help: GPG-sign the push request to update refs on the receiving side, to allow it to be checked by the hooks and/or be logged

tags.help: All refs under refs/tags are pushed, in addition to refspecs explicitly listed on the command line

thin.help: These options are passed to git-send-pack(1)
